topic: The 1954 Asch conformity experiment that revealed group pressure

script.title: Asch conformity experiment shows why we follow the crowd
script.hook: Who decides reality when everyone nods?

scenes.text: Who decides reality when everyone nods?

motion_action.headline: Who decides reality when everyone nods?

scenes.text: In 1951 psychologist Solomon Asch gathered strangers in a room.
He showed them a line and asked which matched a longer one.
One person gave the correct answer, but the rest shouted the wrong length.
About thirty‑seven percent of participants conformed at least once, doubting their own sight.
When a true ally spoke up, conformity dropped to under fifteen percent.
The experiment proves we trust the group over our senses.
Now you know why you second‑guess yourself in crowds:
